messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: service=model-serving canary deployment failure — error rate spike detected in canary group (us-west-2). Triggered paging to #incidents.

sam (oncall): acked. paging rotation: i'm oncall for 30m. looking now.

maya (eng): saw the alert, tailing the canary logs. initial 5xx are all KMS:Decrypt permission denied in logs.

alan (sre): can you paste a snippet of the error?

maya (eng): sure, from the canary pod: ```
2026-03-15T18:02:10Z ERROR model-serving: failed to init credentials: KMS Decrypt error: AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/abcd-rotated-key
```

jorge (release): wait, we rotated KMS key during the deploy pipeline earlier and updated secrets manager with new key id. The canary image still has ENV KMS_KEY_ID=abcd-oldkey. possibility of mismatch.

sam (oncall): that would explain only the canary failing — it picks the new image with baked-in env? Which of the deploy steps writes env?

jorge (release): the helm chart reads KMS key id from the release pipeline env var at render time. Looks like the canary rendering used cached config from previous stage. I'm checking the release job logs now.

liz (support): any customer impact yet? any outbound pages from customers? I'm watching support queue.

maya (eng): quick check across canaries: 3/5 canary pods in us-west-2 failing with same error. Non-canary prod pods in other regions are fine. So limited impact to canary traffic only, but we route a small percent of production traffic to canaries — roughly 2-3% of requests. Error rate for those requests ~100% currently. Overall customer-facing error impact ~2-3% of requests, some customers hitting retries.

alan (sre): good that it's scoped. timeline: we need to stop canary rollouts and rollback the deployment to previous config. Also kill the feature flag that ramps canary traffic.

sam (oncall): deploying rollback now. jorge, please coordinate. I'll keep the channel updated.

jorge (release): running rollback command: ```bash
helm rollback model-serving-release 46 --namespace prod --wait
```

incident-bot: DEPLOYMENT ROLLBACK: model-serving-release -> revision 46 initiated by jorge.

maya (eng): while rollback runs, i'm checking whether the credentials for the new key are missing role binding. quick IAM check: aws iam simulate-principal-policy shows Deny for kms:Decrypt on the new key for the node role. Looks like the KMS key policy wasn't updated to include the node role after rotation.

sam (oncall): so two problems: (1) canary config pointed to old/new mismatched key id, (2) node role lacks permission on new key. which one is root cause?

maya (eng): root cause for immediate failures is permission on key id referenced by pods. If the pods reference a key the node role can't decrypt with, they fail. The mismatch just made some pods point at a key without perms.

alan (sre): rollback completed — canary traffic cut. incident-bot: ROLLBACK COMPLETE.

jorge (release): confirm: traffic back to stable, canary disabled. rolling back the helm values that read env from pipeline cache. will run a hotfix to force env var refresh.

liz (support): i'll send a one-line to customers in the queue if needed: "We're investigating a small subset of requests that saw transient failures during a canary deploy; fix in progress." Any customers already impacted that we should escalate?

sam (oncall): only internal monitoring showed ~2-3% errors, no major customer escalations yet. set status: diminished customer impact, partial.

maya (eng): root cause summary for postmortem: KMS key rotation + release pipeline cached render led to inconsistent KMS_KEY_ID values across canary vs stable. Additionally, the new key's key policy did not include the node role, causing Decrypt AccessDenied.

kai (devex): noted — i'll add a pipeline guard to invalidate cache when kms rotation flag is set, and add a validation step to verify key policy includes node roles before rollout.

jorge (release): for immediate mitigation: (1) rollback completed, (2) we killed canary flag and halted ongoing releases, (3) i'll update pipeline to force env refresh and re-run canary in a dry-run mode once keys/policies are confirmed.

alan (sre): taking an action item: update runbook 'deploy/rotate-kms' to include a preflight check: `aws kms get-key-policy` + `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` for node roles.

sam (oncall): handoff in 20m to next oncall @maya will be primary for follow-up. i'll remain available for escalation.

liz (support): sending note to affected trial customers: "We've reverted a canary deploy that briefly caused errors for a small percentage of requests. No data loss; we will follow up with postmortem"

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: severity=low, impact=partial, status=mitigated.

maya (eng): logging follow-ups to postmortem board and adding timeline. thanks all.

sam (oncall): closing paging loop. leaving channel for follow-up docs.
